question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To deliberately ignore someone or treat them with intentional indifference.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. give someone cold shoulder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "give someone cold shoulder" means to deliberately ignore someone or treat them with intentional indifference.
◦ (किसी की उपेक्षा करना)

• This idiom is informal and widely used in everyday English and is commonly used to describe snubbing a person after a disagreement or falling out. (यह मुहावरा किसी से नाराज़गी के बाद उसे नज़रअंदाज़ करने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. give someone cold shoulder.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: break the ice (माहौल को सहज बनाना): to say or do something that relieves tension or awkwardness, especially when meeting someone for the first time.
◦ Example: He told a joke to break the ice at the meeting.

• Option 3: rub someone the wrong way (किसी को नाराज़ करना): to irritate or annoy someone, often unintentionally.
◦ Example: His blunt comments rubbed his colleagues the wrong way.

• Option 4: see eye to eye (सहमत होना): to agree with someone completely on a matter.
◦ Example: The two partners finally saw eye to eye on the new business plan.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bad patch – Difficult period (कठिन समय)

2. Bite the bullet – To face a difficult situation bravely (कठिन परिस्थिति का साहस से सामना करना)

3. Burn the midnight oil – To work late into the night (देर रात तक कड़ी मेहनत करना)

4. Add fuel to the fire – To worsen a bad situation (स्थिति को और बिगाड़ना)

5. Once in a blue moon – Very rarely (कभी-कभार)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

When the police arrived at the scene, the thief decided to ______ rather than face arrest.
option_1: show a clean pair of hands
option_2: show a clean pair of heels
option_3: show a dirty pair of heels
option_4: show a clean pair of boots
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. show a clean pair of heels.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "show a clean pair of heels" means to run away quickly, especially to escape from danger or an unpleasant situation. (भाग खड़ा होना)
◦ Example: As soon as he saw the guard dog, the burglar showed a clean pair of heels.

 

• The completed sentence reads: When the police arrived at the scene, the thief decided to show a clean pair of heels rather than face arrest. The idiom fits because it describes someone fleeing swiftly to avoid capture.

 

• The expression comes from the visual image of a person running so fast that only the clean soles of their heels are visible to onlookers as they dash away.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "show a clean pair of hands", "show a dirty pair of heels" and "show a clean pair of boots" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing a key word in the genuine idiom (heels → hands/boots, or clean → dirty), and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A close shave – A narrow escape from danger (बाल-बाल बचना)

2. Beat around the bush – To avoid speaking directly about something (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना)

3. Call it a day – To stop doing something for the time being (काम समाप्त करना)

4. Down to earth – Practical and realistic (व्यावहारिक और सरल)

5. Face the music – To accept the consequences of one's actions (परिणाम भुगतना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

To turn over new leaf.
option_1: To quickly skim through the pages of a book
option_2: To become interested in gardening or plants
option_3: To make a fresh start by improving one's behaviour or habits
option_4: To fully recover from a long illness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To make a fresh start by improving one's behaviour or habits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "to turn over new leaf" means to make a fresh start by improving one's behaviour or habits, leaving past mistakes behind. (नई शुरुआत करना)
◦ Example: After failing the exam, he decided to turn over a new leaf and study seriously.

 

• The word "leaf" here refers to a page of a book rather than a plant leaf — the image is of literally turning to a fresh, blank page to begin writing anew, a sense that is often confused with the plant-related literal meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 reflects a literal misreading of "leaf" as a page of a book being skimmed quickly, rather than the idiomatic sense of starting afresh.

 

• Option 2 confuses the idiom with a literal, plant-related reading of "leaf", which has nothing to do with its actual meaning.

 

• Option 4 describes recovering from illness, a meaning often mixed up with unrelated idioms like "turn the corner", not with this idiom.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Get cold feet – To become nervous about doing something (हिम्मत हार जाना)

2. Hit the nail on the head – To describe exactly what is causing a situation (सही बात कहना)

3. In the same boat – Facing the same difficult situation (एक समान स्थिति में होना)

4. Jump on the bandwagon – To join a popular activity or trend (लोकप्रिय काम में शामिल होना)

5. Keep an eye on – To watch carefully (नज़र रखना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To do something with complete strength and determination, using every possible effort.
option_1: at the drop of a hat
option_3: by the skin of one's teeth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. tooth and nail.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "tooth and nail" means with full strength/determination, using every possible effort.
◦ (पूरी ताकत और दृढ़ता के साथ)

• This idiom is a vivid, forceful expression and is commonly used to describe fighting or competing fiercely for something important. (यह मुहावरा किसी महत्वपूर्ण चीज़ के लिए भरसक संघर्ष करने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. tooth and nail.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: at the drop of a hat (तुरंत, बिना देर किए): to do something immediately, without hesitation or a specific reason.
◦ Example: He is ready to help at the drop of a hat.

• Option 2: through thick and thin (हर परिस्थिति में साथ देना): to remain loyal and supportive through both good times and bad.
◦ Example: She stood by her friend through thick and thin.

• Option 3: by the skin of one's teeth (बाल-बाल बचना, बड़ी मुश्किल से): to narrowly succeed at doing something, just barely managing it.
◦ Example: He passed the exam by the skin of his teeth.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Let the cat out of the bag – To reveal a secret accidentally (राज़ खोल देना)

2. Miss the boat – To lose an opportunity by being too slow (मौका चूक जाना)

3. On the ball – Alert and quick to understand (सतर्क और चौकस)

4. Piece of cake – Something very easy to do (बहुत आसान काम)

5. Quick on the uptake – Fast at understanding things (जल्दी समझने वाला)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The teacher used a diagram instead of a lengthy explanation, believing that ______.
option_1: a picture is worth a thousand words
option_3: the pen is mightier than the sword
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a picture is worth a thousand words.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "a picture is worth a thousand words" means a single image can convey complex ideas more effectively than a long description, since visuals communicate meaning instantly. (एक तस्वीर हज़ार शब्दों से बढ़कर होती है)
◦ Example: The company used an infographic instead of a report, knowing a picture is worth a thousand words.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The teacher used a diagram instead of a lengthy explanation, believing that a picture is worth a thousand words. The idiom fits because it directly praises visual explanation over verbal description.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "actions speak louder than words" (deeds are more convincing than promises), "the pen is mightier than the sword" (writing and ideas have more lasting power than violence) and "silence is golden" (staying quiet is often wiser than speaking) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of visual communication being more effective than words required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Rain check – A promise to accept an offer at a later time (बाद के लिए टालना)

2. Sit on the fence – To avoid taking sides in a dispute (तटस्थ रहना)

3. Steal someone's thunder – To take credit for someone else's achievement (किसी की उपलब्धि का श्रेय खुद लेना)

4. Under the weather – Feeling slightly ill (थोड़ा अस्वस्थ महसूस करना)

5. Weather the storm – To survive a difficult period successfully (कठिन समय से सफलतापूर्वक निकलना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Spill the beans.
option_1: To cook a meal carelessly, spilling ingredients everywhere
option_2: To accidentally or carelessly reveal secret information
option_4: To waste money on something unnecessary
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To accidentally or carelessly reveal secret information.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal secret information, often carelessly or accidentally. (राज़ खोल देना)
◦ Example: She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.

 

• The word "spill" carries the special sense of letting something out unintentionally, which is why the idiom is often used when a secret is revealed by mistake rather than on purpose.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 takes the words literally, imagining beans and cooking, which has nothing to do with the idiom's actual meaning.

 

• Option 3 confuses this idiom with expressions about losing one's temper, such as "blow a fuse", which describe anger rather than revealing a secret.

 

• Option 4 wrongly connects the idiom to wasting money, a meaning it does not carry at all.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Bark up the wrong tree – To pursue a mistaken course of action (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना)

2. Cut corners – To do something in the cheapest or easiest way (काम में कोताही करना)

3. Draw a blank – To fail to remember or find something (कुछ याद न आना)

4. Give someone the benefit of the doubt – To trust what someone says without proof (बिना सबूत भरोसा करना)

5. Hold your horses – To wait and be patient (धैर्य रखना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To tease or joke with someone in a playful, good-natured way, often making them believe something untrue for fun.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pull someone's leg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "pull someone's leg" means to tease or joke with someone in a playful, good-natured way, often making them believe something untrue for fun.
◦ (किसी का मज़ाक उड़ाना, हल्के-फुल्के अंदाज़ में चुहल करना)

• This idiom is informal and light-hearted and is commonly used among friends and family to indicate harmless teasing rather than genuine deception. (यह मुहावरा दोस्तों के बीच हल्के-फुल्के मज़ाक के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pull someone's leg.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: get on someone's nerves (किसी को चिढ़ाना/परेशान करना): to irritate or annoy someone repeatedly.
◦ Example: His loud music gets on his neighbour's nerves every night.

• Option 2: add insult to injury (घाव पर नमक छिड़कना): to make a bad situation even worse for someone.
◦ Example: Losing his job was bad enough, but being fined too added insult to injury.

• Option 4: put one's foot in it (अनजाने में गलत बात कह देना): to say something embarrassing or tactless by mistake.
◦ Example: He really put his foot in it when he asked about her ex-husband at the party.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. In hot water – In a difficult or troublesome situation (मुसीबत में)

2. Jump the gun – To act too soon, before the right time (समय से पहले कार्य करना)

3. Keep something at bay – To prevent something from approaching or affecting you (दूर रखना)

4. Learn the ropes – To learn how to do a job properly (काम सीखना)

5. Make ends meet – To have just enough money to live on (गुज़ारा करना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

You haven't even received the offer letter yet, so ______ — wait until it's confirmed.
option_1: don't put all your eggs in one basket
option_3: don't judge a book by its cover
option_4: don't count your chickens before they hatch
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. don't count your chickens before they hatch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "don't count your chickens before they hatch" means you should not assume something will happen or plan around a benefit before it is certain. (काम पूरा होने से पहले उसके परिणाम की उम्मीद मत करो)
◦ Example: He already planned to buy a car with his bonus, but I told him not to count his chickens before they hatch.

 

• The completed sentence reads: You haven't even received the offer letter yet, so don't count your chickens before they hatch — wait until it's confirmed. The idiom fits because it warns against assuming a good outcome before it is officially certain.

 

• The expression comes from the old farming caution that chicken eggs may not all hatch successfully, so counting the chickens beforehand could lead to a false, premature calculation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "don't put all your eggs in one basket" (don't risk everything on a single plan), "don't cry over spilt milk" (don't regret something that has already happened and cannot be changed) and "don't judge a book by its cover" (don't form an opinion based only on appearance) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of not assuming an uncertain future outcome required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Method to one's madness – A reasonable purpose behind seemingly odd behaviour (पागलपन में भी एक तरीका होना)

2. Nip something in the bud – To stop a problem at an early stage (शुरुआत में ही रोक देना)

3. Off the hook – No longer responsible or blamed for something (जिम्मेदारी से मुक्त)

4. Pass the buck – To shift responsibility or blame to someone else (जिम्मेदारी टालना)

5. Read between the lines – To understand a hidden meaning (छिपे हुए अर्थ को समझना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

White elephant.
option_1: A possession that is costly to maintain but of little use or value
option_2: A rare and highly prized animal kept in a zoo
option_3: A person who stands out awkwardly in a group
option_4: A large, successful, and highly profitable business venture
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A possession that is costly to maintain but of little use or value.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "white elephant" means a possession that is expensive or troublesome to maintain but provides little use or benefit. (एक ऐसी वस्तु जो रखने में महंगी हो पर उपयोगी न हो, फ़िज़ूल का बोझ)
◦ Example: The unused stadium became a white elephant, costing the city millions in upkeep every year.

 

• The phrase originates from the practice of Southeast Asian kings gifting rare white elephants to courtiers they wished to burden financially, since the sacred animals could not be put to work yet were extremely costly to keep.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 takes the phrase literally as a real, rare animal rather than its idiomatic sense of a costly burden.

 

• Option 3 confuses this idiom with the unrelated expression "elephant in the room", which refers to an obvious problem nobody wants to discuss.

 

• Option 4 describes the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning, since a white elephant is a drain on resources, not a profitable asset.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Run out of steam – To lose energy or enthusiasm to continue (उत्साह या ऊर्जा खत्म हो जाना)

2. Save for a rainy day – To save money for future difficulties (मुश्किल समय के लिए बचत करना)

3. Sit tight – To wait patiently without taking action (धैर्यपूर्वक इंतज़ार करना)

4. Take something with a pinch of salt – To not fully believe something (पूरी तरह विश्वास न करना)

5. Turn a blind eye – To deliberately ignore something (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To feel regret or complain uselessly about something bad that has already happened and cannot be undone.
option_4: bite off more than one can chew
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cry over split milk.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "cry over split milk" means to feel regret or complain uselessly about something bad that has already happened and cannot be undone.
◦ (बीती बात पर पछताना, जो हो गया उस पर रोना)

• This idiom is a classic exam idiom and is commonly used to advise someone to accept a past mistake and move forward instead of dwelling on it. (यह मुहावरा बीती बात पर पछताने के बजाय आगे बढ़ने की सलाह देने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cry over split milk.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: let bygones be bygones (बीती बातों को भुला देना): to forgive past disagreements and not let them affect the present relationship.
◦ Example: The two brothers decided to let bygones be bygones and started talking again.

• Option 3: burn one's bridges (ऐसे संबंध तोड़ना जिन्हें फिर से न जोड़ा जा सके): to destroy all possibility of returning to a previous situation or relationship.
◦ Example: He burned his bridges when he insulted his boss on his last day.

• Option 4: bite off more than one can chew (अपनी क्षमता से अधिक काम अपने ऊपर ले लेना): to take on a task that is too difficult or too much to handle.
◦ Example: Agreeing to organize the entire event alone, she bit off more than she could chew.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Cut to the chase – To get to the point without wasting time (सीधे मुद्दे पर आना)

2. Every cloud has a silver lining – Something good can come from a bad situation (हर बुरी स्थिति में कुछ अच्छा छिपा होता है)

3. Fall on hard times – To experience a period of financial difficulty (आर्थिक कठिनाई का सामना करना)

4. Give someone a piece of one's mind – To scold someone angrily (किसी को खरी-खोटी सुनाना)

5. Hit the sack – To go to bed (सोने जाना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The investigating team promised to ______ in order to find the missing child.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. leave no stone unturned.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "leave no stone unturned" means to try every possible means to achieve something or solve a problem, making a thorough and complete effort. (कोई कसर न छोड़ना, हर संभव प्रयास करना)
◦ Example: The company left no stone unturned in its search for a solution to the production delay.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The investigating team promised to leave no stone unturned in order to find the missing child. The idiom fits because it expresses a commitment to use every possible method in the search.

 

• The expression is believed to originate from an ancient Greek legend in which an oracle advised a general to search thoroughly beneath every stone on a battlefield to find a hidden treasure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "leave no brick unturned", "leave no leaf unturned" and "leave no pebble unturned" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing "stone" with another object (brick, leaf, or pebble), and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Kick the bucket – To die (मर जाना)

2. Lose one's train of thought – To forget what one was saying (बात भूल जाना)

3. Make a mountain out of a molehill – To exaggerate a minor problem (छोटी बात को बड़ा बना देना)

4. No pain, no gain – Success requires effort and sacrifice (मेहनत के बिना फल नहीं मिलता)

5. On cloud nine – Extremely happy (बहुत खुश)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Cut no ice.
option_1: To move very quickly and easily through something
option_2: To have a strong and decisive influence on a decision
option_3: To break the initial awkwardness in a social situation
option_4: To fail to make any impression or have any effect on someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To fail to make any impression or have any effect on someone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "cut no ice" means to fail to make any impression or have any influence on someone, however hard one tries. (कोई असर न डालना)
◦ Example: His endless excuses cut no ice with the principal, who suspended him anyway.

 

• The word "ice" stands for a mark or impression that would normally be cut into a surface; when nothing gets cut, nothing has registered — this idiom is often wrongly confused with the unrelated idiom "break the ice".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes literal, effortless movement, mistaking the figurative sense of "cutting" for a physical one.

 

• Option 2 states the direct opposite of the idiom, which specifically denotes an ABSENCE of influence, not a strong one.

 

• Option 3 is actually the meaning of the unrelated idiom "break the ice", used for easing social tension rather than failing to impress.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bad patch – Difficult period (कठिन समय)

2. A bolt from the blue – A sudden shock (अचानक आघात)

3. A bone of contention – A cause of dispute (विवाद का कारण)

4. A close shave – A narrow escape (बाल-बाल बचना)

5. A far cry – Very different from (बहुत भिन्न)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To attempt any possible means, however unlikely to succeed, out of sheer desperation.
option_2: burn the candle at both ends
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. grasp at straws.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "grasp at straws" means to attempt any possible means, however unlikely to succeed, out of sheer desperation.
◦ (तिनके का सहारा लेना)

• This idiom is a vivid, classic exam idiom and is commonly used to describe a person clinging to a hopeless plan when all better options have failed. (निराशा में असंभव उपाय अपनाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. grasp at straws.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: burn the candle at both ends (दोनों ओर से मेहनत करके स्वयं को थका देना): to exhaust oneself by working excessively, often at both day and night.
◦ Example: Preparing for two exams together, she was burning the candle at both ends.

• Option 3: beat around the bush (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना): to avoid talking about something directly.
◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me the real reason.

• Option 4: rest on one's laurels (अपनी पुरानी सफलता पर संतुष्ट हो जाना): to become complacent because of past success and stop trying further.
◦ Example: Despite winning last year, the team did not rest on its laurels.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A leopard cannot change its spots – One cannot change one's basic nature (स्वभाव नहीं बदलता)

2. A man of straw – A person of no substance (तुच्छ व्यक्ति)

3. A pain in the neck – An annoying person or thing (सिरदर्द बनना)

4. A piece of cake – A very easy task (बहुत आसान काम)

5. A red letter day – A memorable day (यादगार दिन)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

Ever since the property dispute, the two brothers have been ______ with each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. at daggers drawn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "at daggers drawn" means in a state of open, bitter hostility with someone, ready for a serious quarrel. (घोर शत्रुता में होना)
◦ Example: The two political rivals have been at daggers drawn since the last election.

 

• The completed sentence reads: Ever since the property dispute, the two brothers have been at daggers drawn with each other. This fits because the sentence describes an ongoing, bitter conflict between them, not mere confusion or distance.

 

• The expression comes from the literal image of two people standing with daggers drawn, ready to fight — a picture of open enmity that has long been used figuratively in English.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "at loose ends" (having nothing particular to do), "at arm's length" (keeping someone at a cautious distance) and "at sixes and sevens" (in a state of confusion or disorder) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of open, bitter hostility required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A slap on the wrist – A very mild punishment (हल्की सजा)

2. A storm in a teacup – Great fuss over a trivial matter (बात का बतंगड़)

3. A wet blanket – A person who spoils others' enjoyment (मज़ा किरकिरा करने वाला)

4. Add fuel to the fire – To worsen a situation (आग में घी डालना)

5. All ears – Listening attentively (ध्यान से सुनना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Jump the gun.
option_1: To start a race with a sudden burst of speed
option_2: To become extremely excited about an upcoming event
option_3: To act before the appropriate or proper time
option_4: To make a loud and sudden noise to attract attention
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To act before the appropriate or proper time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "jump the gun" means to act before the proper or appropriate time, often without adequate preparation or authorisation. (समय से पहले कार्य करना)
◦ Example: The company jumped the gun by announcing the merger before the deal was finalised.

 

• The phrase originates from athletics, where a runner who starts before the starter's gun is fired is said to have "jumped the gun"; the idiom keeps this sense of premature action in everyday usage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes literal sprinting at the start of a race, missing the figurative sense of acting too early.

 

• Option 2 confuses premature action with mere excitement, which is not what the idiom conveys.

 

• Option 4 takes the word "gun" literally as a loud noise-maker, ignoring the idiom's figurative meaning of premature timing.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. An axe to grind – A personal, selfish motive (स्वार्थ साधना)

2. Back to the drawing board – To start over (नए सिरे से शुरू करना)

3. Bark up the wrong tree – To pursue a mistaken course (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना)

4. Beat about the bush – To avoid the main point (इधर-उधर की बात करना)

5. Bite the bullet – To face a difficulty bravely (कठिनाई का सामना करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To waste time and energy on something that has no chance of success or is already finished.
option_2: put the cart before the horse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. be a dead horse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "be a dead horse" means to waste time and energy on something that has no chance of success or is already finished.
◦ (बेकार की मेहनत करना)

• This idiom is a classic exam idiom and is commonly used to warn against continuing to pursue a lost cause or a matter that has already been settled. (समाप्त हो चुके विषय पर व्यर्थ प्रयास करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. be a dead horse.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: burn the midnight oil (देर रात तक काम करना): to work or study late into the night.
◦ Example: She burned the midnight oil for a week before her final exams.

• Option 2: put the cart before the horse (काम को उल्टे क्रम में करना): to do things in the wrong order, reversing the natural sequence.
◦ Example: Planning the party before confirming the venue is putting the cart before the horse.

• Option 3: get the lion's share (सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा पाना): to receive the largest part of something.
◦ Example: The eldest son got the lion's share of the property.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Bite the dust – To fail or be defeated (हार जाना)

2. Blow one's own trumpet – To boast about oneself (अपनी तारीफ खुद करना)

3. Break the ice – To ease tension in a social setting (बातचीत की शुरुआत करना)

4. By hook or by crook – By any means (जैसे भी हो)

5. Call it a day – To stop working (काम बंद करना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

After the argument, she gave her old friend ______ at the party, refusing even to say hello.
option_4: A taste of her own medicine
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A cold shoulder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "a cold shoulder" means to deliberately ignore or treat someone with indifference, especially someone who expects a warm welcome. (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना)
◦ Example: When he apologised, his colleagues still gave him a cold shoulder for weeks.

 

• The completed sentence reads: After the argument, she gave her old friend a cold shoulder at the party, refusing even to say hello. This fits because the sentence describes deliberate indifference, not anger expressed aloud or revenge.

 

• The expression is said to come from the old custom of serving an unwelcome guest a cold shoulder of mutton instead of a hot meal, as a polite but unmistakable sign of displeasure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "the benefit of the doubt" (assuming something positive about someone despite incomplete evidence), "a piece of her mind" (an angry, frank rebuke) and "a taste of her own medicine" (retaliating against someone in the same way they treated others) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of silent indifference required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Call a spade a spade – To speak frankly (साफ-साफ बात कहना)

2. Castles in the air – Impractical dreams (हवाई किले)

3. Cost an arm and a leg – Very expensive (बहुत महंगा)

4. Cut corners – To do something cheaply/carelessly (काम में कोताही बरतना)

5. Draw a blank – To get no result (कुछ हासिल न होना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Cry wolf.
option_1: To shout loudly in fear during a genuine emergency
option_2: To raise a false alarm so often that a real one is not believed
option_3: To howl in imitation of a wild animal
option_4: To warn someone about a real and imminent danger
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To raise a false alarm so often that a real one is not believed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "cry wolf" means to raise a false alarm, especially so often that people stop believing a warning even when it turns out to be true. (झूठी चेतावनी देना)
◦ Example: After crying wolf twice about theft in the office, no one believed him when the laptop was actually stolen.

 

• The idiom comes from Aesop's fable of the shepherd boy who repeatedly tricked villagers by falsely shouting that a wolf was attacking his flock, so when a wolf genuinely appeared, no one came to help.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 wrongly assumes the alarm in this idiom is genuine, whereas the idiom specifically refers to a FALSE alarm.

 

• Option 3 takes the word "wolf" literally as an animal sound, missing the idiom's figurative meaning about false warnings.

 

• Option 4 describes a genuine, real warning, which is essentially the opposite of the idiom's meaning of a false one.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Face the music – To accept unpleasant consequences (परिणाम भुगतना)

2. Feather in one's cap – An achievement to be proud of (गौरव की बात)

3. Fish out of water – Uncomfortable in a situation (असहज महसूस करना)

4. Get cold feet – To become nervous before an event (हिम्मत हार जाना)

5. Go the extra mile – To make additional effort (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To confess something fully and honestly, holding nothing back, usually to relieve one's conscience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. make a clean breast of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "make a clean breast of" means to confess something fully and honestly, holding nothing back, usually to relieve one's conscience.
◦ (पूरी सच्चाई स्वीकार कर लेना)

• This idiom is a somewhat formal, classic exam idiom and is commonly used when someone admits a wrongdoing or a long-held secret openly. (खुलकर अपराध या राज़ स्वीकार करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. make a clean breast of.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: keep something under wraps (गुप्त रखना): to keep something secret or hidden from others.
◦ Example: The company kept its new product under wraps until the launch event.

• Option 2: beat a hasty retreat (जल्दी से पीछे हट जाना): to leave a place or situation quickly, especially to avoid trouble.
◦ Example: Seeing the angry crowd, the salesman beat a hasty retreat.

• Option 4: throw in the towel (हार मान लेना): to give up on an effort, admitting defeat.
◦ Example: After three failed attempts, he finally threw in the towel.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Hang by a thread – In a precarious situation (नाज़ुक स्थिति में होना)

2. Hit the nail on the head – To describe exactly what is causing a situation (सही बात कहना)

3. In the same boat – In the same difficult situation (एक ही स्थिति में होना)

4. Keep one's fingers crossed – To hope for good luck (शुभकामना करना)

5. Kill two birds with one stone – To achieve two things with one action (एक तीर से दो शिकार)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The employees decided to ______ for one day to warn the management before launching a full-scale agitation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. take strike.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "take strike" means to hold a brief, token strike as a warning, before deciding whether to launch a longer or full-scale strike. (चेतावनी स्वरूप हड़ताल करना)
◦ Example: The transport workers decided to take strike for a day to press their demand for higher wages.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The employees decided to take strike for one day to warn the management before launching a full-scale agitation. This fits because the sentence explicitly describes a short warning action before a bigger step, matching the idiom's meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "call it quits" (to stop an activity or effort altogether), "toe the line" (to conform strictly to rules or expectations) and "burn their boats" (to commit to a course of action leaving no way back) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of a short, warning-style strike required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Let the cat out of the bag – To reveal a secret (राज़ खोलना)

2. Once in a blue moon – Very rarely (कभी-कभार)

3. On cloud nine – Extremely happy (बहुत खुश)

4. Pull someone's leg – To joke with someone (मज़ाक करना)

5. Rain cats and dogs – To rain heavily (मूसलधार बारिश)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Bury the hatchet.
option_1: To end a quarrel and make peace with someone
option_2: To dig up old, forgotten arguments
option_3: To hide an important weapon or tool
option_4: To work extremely hard on a difficult task
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To end a quarrel and make peace with someone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to end a quarrel or conflict and make peace with someone, agreeing to forget past differences. (आपसी झगड़ा भुलाकर मेल-मिलाप कर लेना)
◦ Example: The two neighbours finally buried the hatchet after years of dispute over the boundary wall.

 

• The phrase comes from a Native American tradition of literally burying a hatchet, or tomahawk, as a symbol of peace after a conflict; English retains it purely in this figurative sense of reconciliation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 wrongly reverses the idiom's direction — burying something means putting it away for good, not digging up old grievances.

 

• Option 3 takes the word "hatchet" literally as a physical weapon being hidden, missing the idiom's figurative sense of reconciliation.

 

• Option 4 describes hard work, which has no connection to the idiom's actual meaning of making peace after a quarrel.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Read between the lines – To understand hidden meaning (गूढ़ अर्थ समझना)

2. See eye to eye – To agree completely (सहमत होना)

3. Show one's true colours – To reveal one's real character (असली रूप दिखाना)

4. Sit on the fence – To remain neutral (तटस्थ रहना)

5. Spill the beans – To reveal secret information (भेद खोलना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To say clearly and directly what one means, without wasting time on unnecessary details.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. get to the point.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get to the point" means to say clearly and directly what one means, without wasting time on unnecessary details.
◦ (सीधे मुद्दे पर आना)

• This idiom is a common, everyday idiom and is commonly used to urge someone to stop giving a long-winded explanation and state their main point. (बिना घुमाए सीधी बात कहना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. get to the point.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: beat around the bush (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना): to avoid talking about the main subject directly.
◦ Example: He kept beating around the bush instead of answering the question directly.

• Option 3: let sleeping dogs lie (पुरानी बात को न छेड़ना): to avoid interfering with a situation that could cause trouble if disturbed.
◦ Example: They decided to let sleeping dogs lie and not reopen the old dispute.

• Option 4: split hairs (बाल की खाल निकालना): to make unnecessarily fine distinctions in an argument.
◦ Example: The lawyers were splitting hairs over the exact wording of the contract.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Steal someone's thunder – To take credit for another's achievement (किसी का श्रेय छीनना)

2. Take with a pinch of salt – To not fully believe (पूरी तरह विश्वास न करना)

3. The last straw – The final problem that causes a collapse (सहनशीलता की अंतिम सीमा)

4. Turn a blind eye – To ignore deliberately (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना)

5. Under the weather – Feeling slightly ill (तबियत ठीक न होना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

It takes real courage to ______ in a room full of people who strongly disagree with you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. speak your mind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "speak your mind" means to express your opinions openly and honestly, even if they are blunt or unpopular. (अपने विचार बेझिझक और स्पष्ट रूप से व्यक्त करना)
◦ Example: During the debate, she didn't hesitate to speak her mind about the flawed policy.

 

• The completed sentence reads: It takes real courage to speak your mind in a room full of people who strongly disagree with you. The idiom fits because the sentence is about openly expressing an opinion despite opposition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "hold your tongue" (to deliberately stay silent), "beat around the bush" (to avoid coming to the point directly) and "bite your tongue" (to stop yourself from saying something, often out of restraint) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of open, honest expression required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bad patch – A difficult period (कठिन समय)

2. Add fuel to the fire – To worsen an already bad situation (आग में घी डालना)

3. At the drop of a hat – Immediately, without hesitation (तुरंत, बिना देर किए)

4. Burn the midnight oil – To work or study late into the night (देर रात तक मेहनत करना)

5. By hook or by crook – By any means necessary (किसी भी तरह से)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Jack up the rates.
option_1: To lower prices temporarily to attract customers.
option_2: To fix a maximum limit on prices set by the government.
option_3: To calculate the average price of a commodity over time.
option_4: To increase prices sharply and often unfairly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To increase prices sharply and often unfairly..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "jack up the rates" means to increase prices sharply, often steeply and without much justification. (कीमतों को अचानक और तेज़ी से बढ़ा देना)
◦ Example: During the festival season, many shopkeepers jack up the rates of essential goods.

 

• The verb "jack up" literally means to raise something using a mechanical jack, and here it is used figuratively for a sudden, sharp rise in price rather than a small or gradual increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes a price cut, which is the opposite of what "jack up" means.

 

• Option 2 confuses the idiom with price regulation or capping, which is not what "jack up" refers to.

 

• Option 3 wrongly treats the idiom as a neutral statistical exercise rather than an active, deliberate price increase.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Call it a day – To stop doing something for the day (दिन भर के लिए काम बंद करना)

2. Cut corners – To do something poorly or cheaply to save time or money (काम में कोताही करना)

3. Down in the dumps – Feeling very sad or depressed (बहुत उदास होना)

4. Draw a blank – To fail to get any result or response (कोई परिणाम या जवाब न मिलना)

5. Fish out of water – Uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings (अनजान परिस्थितियों में असहज महसूस करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Hoping for something to work out or succeed even though there is very little or no real chance of it happening, driven by desperation rather than reason.
option_2: Hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. clutching at straws.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "clutching at straws" means hoping for something to succeed even though there is very little or no real chance of it happening, out of desperation rather than reason.
◦ (निराशा की स्थिति में बिना किसी ठोस आधार के आशा करना)

• This idiom is a vivid, informal metaphor and is commonly used to describe someone who refuses to give up hope even when a situation looks nearly lost. (एक ऐसे व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग होता है जो लगभग निराश स्थिति में भी आशा नहीं छोड़ता)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. clutching at straws.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: Hit the nail on the head (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना): to describe or identify something exactly and accurately.
◦ Example: Her analysis of the problem hit the nail on the head.

• Option 3: Bite the bullet (कठिनाई का साहस से सामना करना): to face a difficult or unpleasant situation bravely because it cannot be avoided.
◦ Example: After months of delay, he finally bit the bullet and resigned from the toxic workplace.

• Option 4: Cast pearls before swine (अयोग्य व्यक्ति को कीमती वस्तु देना): to offer something valuable to someone who cannot appreciate or use it.
◦ Example: Giving him financial advice is like casting pearls before swine; he never listens.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Get cold feet – To become nervous and hesitant about doing something (किसी काम से पहले घबरा जाना)

2. Give the benefit of the doubt – To believe someone's claim without proof against it (शक का लाभ देना)

3. In hot water – To be in trouble (मुसीबत में होना)

4. Keep an eye on – To watch someone or something carefully (किसी पर नज़र रखना)

5. Kill two birds with one stone – To achieve two objectives with a single action (एक तीर से दो शिकार करना)
